content: ext4 vs f2fs on embedded Linux: F2FS is log-structured/checkpoint-based, optimized for flash wear-leveling on SD/eMMC, but multiple sources (LeMaker blog, Gentoo forums, Kevin Locke's SD card writeup) agree it is comparatively weaker under sudden power loss than ext4's mature journal-replay recovery; fsck.f2fs cannot run against a mounted fs (needs initramfs-based repair). ext4 remains the safer default for power-loss tolerance; F2FS's advantage (wear-leveling) matters less on NVMe than on SD/eMMC.
